Sedjem 0.3.2 can send a recording to another computer of yours on the same network and transcribe it there, links
each recording's runs from *Run again*, sorts the list of transcriptions, and makes *Update now* on Windows wait
for the old Sedjem to quit before it replaces it.

## Download

- Windows 10 and 11: `Sedjem-0.3.2-setup.exe` installs for your user, without admin rights. It isn't
  signed yet, so SmartScreen warns about an unknown publisher: choose *More info*, then *Run anyway*.
  Installing over 0.3.1 keeps your transcriptions, keys and models.
- Linux (x64): unpack `Sedjem-0.3.2-linux-x64.tar.gz` and run `Sedjem/Sedjem`.
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` has the checksums of both.

0.3.1 can update itself: *Settings → Updates*, then *Update now*.

## Run on another computer

- A laptop without a graphics card can send a recording to another computer of yours that has one, on the same
  network or over Tailscale, and get the transcript back, line by line as it is made.
- On the computer that will do the work, turn on *Settings → Other computers → Run jobs for other computers* and
  show a pairing code. On the other, type its address and the code once. *New transcription* and *Run again* then
  have *Run on*, and the form asks before the first recording goes to each computer.
- It is off by default. The two computers talk over an encrypted connection, check each other with the one-time
  code and then with the certificate and a token, and only on private addresses. The recording is kept apart from
  the other computer's own library and deleted there once the transcript is back. Everything that travels is in
  the [privacy policy](https://github.com/MohammedEl-sayedAhmed/sedjem/blob/main/docs/privacy.md), and how it works
  in [running jobs on another computer](https://github.com/MohammedEl-sayedAhmed/sedjem/blob/main/docs/15-remote-runs.md).

## The list and Run again

- The list of transcriptions sorts by newest or oldest, title, length, last change or the date the recording was
  made, and remembers the choice.
- *Run again with* shows which models already ran on the recording and links to their transcripts.

## Windows

- *Update now* no longer fails when the installer reaches Sedjem's files before the old Sedjem has quit: it waits
  for it, up to a minute.
- An installation by hand has a Privacy page after the licence, with what Sedjem sends and the box for the
  anonymous usage counts. Its choice is the same as the switch in *Settings → About*.
- The installer and Sedjem.exe show their version and publisher in the file's properties.

## Other fixes

- A model download that finished while its status was being read no longer showed an error for a moment.
- A copy of Sedjem run from its source code, pulled by hand past the version *Update now* offered, starts again
  on its own code instead of failing.

## Known limits

- Running on another computer is new. Its tests run two copies of Sedjem on one computer; it hasn't been tried
  between two computers on many networks yet. The first time it is turned on, Windows asks whether to let Sedjem
  through its firewall: allow it on private networks only.
- The installer is unsigned, and macOS isn't built.
- On Linux, *Update now* unpacks the new build next to the old one rather than replacing it.
- Nemotron-3-Diarization hears at most 8 speakers.
